relevance_note: Case series of four patients each with a TNFAIP3 variant, e.g. '“A” is a 10-year-old girl with heterozygous mutation TNFAIP3 c.740C > T (p.Pro247Leu)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (case presentations, Table 1, Discussion); no supplementary section is present in the Markdown. Rows were written by hand into a Python build script in the scratch directory; every span was copied from the paper by a lookup that keeps the paper's own characters (the paper uses four-per-em spaces before units and thin spaces in 'c.740C > T'; the variant strings for A keep those thin spaces). Table 1 has patients as rows; its spans quote from the patient label. Scope: the four case patients A-D; relatives described with a TNFAIP3 variant, an HA20 diagnosis, an HA20-like feature or autoimmune disease, or a parental test result (D's parents tested negative; they get individual rows but no variant rows); and previously published individuals described with individual-level detail in the Discussion (refs (15, 16), (2, 12, 22), (24), (26), plus the mother and grandmother of the ref (26) patient). Left out: untested relatives described only as unaffected or with conditions the paper does not frame as HA20-related (A's unaffected brother and sister with neurodevelopmental delay; A's parents; B's mother and her second brother; C's unaffected sisters; D's brother with anxiety and epilepsy), and group-level mentions (e.g. 'patients with primary breast marginal zone lymphomas (25)', 'several patients' with p.Arg271*). Labels: the paper uses the letters A-D most often (also 'Patient A', 'Case 1'). Ambiguities: (1) 'identified in a patient with both HA20 and DLBCL, as found in the father of patient B (24)' can be read as ref (24) describing B's father; it was read as a separate earlier patient, so 'ref (24) patient' and 'father of B' are separate rows and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null rather than true or false. (2) B's father is recorded with B's variant because the paper says he has 'the same genetic variant'; his zygosity and B's inheritance are left 'not reported' because neither is stated outright. (3) B's paternal grandfather 'also had HA20' but no variant or testing is stated for him, so he has no variant row. (4) 'nonsense' for B, C and D is taken from 'Three out of four patients had non-sense mutations' plus A's missense variant. (5) The authors' pathogenicity statements for p.Trp168* and p.Q379* cite ClinVar RCV accessions in the paper text; they are recorded verbatim as printed and may need handling in concordance. (6) D's age at HA20 diagnosis is not stated (testing followed a presentation at 13 years), so it is 'not reported'. (7) D's CRP of 60.9 mg/L is not labelled 'elevated' in the text; it was recorded as observed for elevated inflammatory markers. Checklist calls worth review: A 'growth failure' observed from 'poor weight gain'; A's 'negative for uveitis and retinal vasculitis' does not exclude the broader ocular-inflammation or vasculitis items; B's IBD/celiac exclusion does not exclude GI inflammation; father of B and ref (24) patient: DLBCL counted as lymphoproliferation; father of B 'aphthous ulcers' counted as oral ulcers and 'significant cutaneous findings' as skin lesions; great-grandmother's 'joint issues' left not reported for arthritis/arthralgia; D's interstitial lung disease excluded from 'pulmonary computed tomography (CT) scans were normal'; father of D's diverticulitis counted as GI inflammation; 'otherwise healthy' (brother of B) and 'unaffected' (mother of D) were not used to exclude specific features. HLA B51 negativity in C was not recorded (not a TNFAIP3 variant or a phenotype). No internal contradictions found.
